Fit a two-level profile model in two stages, holding the profiles fixed while the group classes are estimated

Source: R/fixed-measurement.R
fit_staged.Rd

fit_staged() fits a two-level profile model in two stages. The first stage estimates the profiles with one group class; the second holds their measurement parameters (means and covariances of continuous indicators, response probabilities of categorical ones) fixed and estimates the profile probabilities within each group class and the group-class proportions. The profiles therefore keep one definition while the group classes differ in composition. A fitted measurement model can be supplied instead of the first stage, to reuse established profiles. The result holds the second-stage estimates and keeps the first-stage fit.

Information criteria and likelihood-ratio comparisons condition on the held measurement. Staged fits that hold the same measurement are compared on n_parameters. A comparison with a jointly estimated fit uses n_parameters_with_measurement and stays descriptive, since staged estimates do not maximise the joint likelihood. Wald standard errors omit the uncertainty of the first stage. parameter_inference(fit, method = "bootstrap") resamples groups and re-estimates both stages (a supplied same-sample measurement model with its own options), so that uncertainty is propagated and the measurement parameters get intervals too. A measurement fitted to different observations, or with unknown provenance, is refused by this bootstrap; resampling the current data cannot represent uncertainty from an external measurement sample.

Usage

fit_staged(
  data,
  vars,
  id,
  n_profiles,
  n_group_classes = 2L,
  measurement = NULL,
  variance_model = c("varying", "equal"),
  n_starts = 10L,
  max_iter = 1000L,
  tol = 1e-08,
  min_variance = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  missing = c("error", "fiml"),
  covariance_model = c("diagonal", "full"),
  categorical = character(),
  min_probability = 1e-10,
  time = NULL,
  search = NULL,
  n_screen = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with the indicators and the group identifier.

vars

Names of the indicator columns. Those not named in categorical are continuous.

id

Name of the group identifier column (character, factor or numeric, without missing values). Required: a staged fit is a two-level model.

n_profiles

Number of individual profiles.

n_group_classes

Number of group classes in the second stage, at least two (default 2).

measurement

Where the profiles come from:

  • NULL (default): the first stage is estimated from data, with one group class;

  • a fitted multilpa model: its measurement estimates are used and only the second stage is estimated. It must have one group class and the same profiles, indicators and measurement options as this call. Its covariance structure must be EEI, VVI, EEE or VVV, and it must not have weights, centering, scaling, ordinal or count indicators, direct_effects, local_dependence or noise.

variance_model, covariance_model

The covariance structure of the continuous indicators, as under multilpa(): variance_model is "varying" (default, variances per profile) or "equal" (shared by all profiles), and covariance_model is "diagonal" (default, no within-profile covariances) or "full". These give the structures VVI, EEI, VVV and EEE; a staged fit takes no other structure.

n_starts

Number of EM starts in each estimated stage (default 10). With measurement, only the second stage is estimated.

max_iter

Maximum EM updates per start in each stage (default 1000); zero evaluates the starting values without updating them.

tol

Convergence tolerance (default 1e-8), per observed indicator value: EM stops when a step changes the log likelihood by no more than tol times the number of observed indicator values.

min_variance

Lower bound on every variance (on every covariance eigenvalue under full covariance), as in multilpa(), applied in both stages; a supplied measurement must satisfy it.

seed

Optional integer seed. The caller's random-number state is restored on exit.

missing

What to do with missing indicator values, in both stages:

  • "error" (default): stop, naming the indicators that have them;

  • "fiml": keep every row and fit each one on the indicators it observes (full-information maximum likelihood), valid when the missingness depends only on observed values.

categorical

Indicators modelled by profile-specific response probabilities over their observed categories, the latent class measurement model. Binary, ordered and unordered indicators share this parameterization. Naming a subset of vars fits a mixed-mode model.

min_probability

Lower bound on every categorical response probability (default 1e-10).

time

Optional column giving each row's occasion within its group, used only to order the rows for get_results(x, "sequences"), "sequence_summary" and plot_sequences(). Values must be unique within a group and sort in their intended order (numbers numerically, factors by level, text alphabetically, so "T2", "T10" is refused: use a factor or zero-pad).

search

How the starting values of each estimated stage are searched, as under multilpa():

  • "kmeans": every one of the n_starts starts is run to convergence;

  • "emEM": a larger pool of n_screen starts is screened with a short EM run each, and only the first start and the best of the rest, n_starts in all, are run to convergence;

  • NULL (default): "emEM" for continuous indicators with a shared covariance matrix (EEI or EEE), "kmeans" otherwise.

The second stage starts from the first-stage measurement and holds it.

n_screen

For search = "emEM" only, the size of the screened pool (default five times n_starts, at least n_starts). The second stage skips screening when n_starts = 1.

Value

A fitted model of class multilpa: the second-stage fit, whose measurement parameters equal the first-stage estimates. Every table, plot and diagnostic of a multilpa() fit applies. What a staged fit adds:

  • get_results(fit, what = "stages"): two rows, measurement (the first stage) and membership (the second), each with its number of group classes, the held blocks (fixed), log_likelihood, parameters, parameters_with_measurement and converged;

  • get_results(fit, what = "profile_probabilities"): the profile proportions within each group class, the result of the second stage;

  • n_parameters counts the second-stage parameters only, which the information criteria use; n_parameters_with_measurement adds the held measurement parameters.

Conditions

latents_bad_argument for n_group_classes below two, id = NULL, or a measurement that is not a multilpa fit; latents_bad_stage for a measurement with group classes, with a different number of profiles, other indicators, categories or covariance structure than this call, or with an option the second stage does not use (listed under measurement); latents_unsupported_noise for a measurement with a noise component. Both stages raise the conditions of multilpa().

See also

multilpa() for holding chosen blocks through fixed; starting_values(fit, what = "measurement") to extract measurement parameters for a later fit.

Examples

# Stage 1: profiles of course sessions. Stage 2: classes of students that
# differ in how often their sessions are in each profile.
staged <- fit_staged(course_engagement, c("browse", "lectures"),
                     id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2,
                     n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
get_results(staged, what = "stages")
#>         stage group_classes            fixed log_likelihood parameters
#> 1 measurement             1             <NA>      -3894.214          9
#> 2  membership             2 means, variances      -3800.754          3
#>   parameters_with_measurement converged
#> 1                           9      TRUE
#> 2                          11      TRUE
get_results(staged, what = "profile_probabilities")
#>   group_class profile probability group_class_probability
#> 1           1       1   0.7840790               0.6747345
#> 2           1       2   0.2159210               0.6747345
#> 3           2       1   0.1792617               0.3252655
#> 4           2       2   0.8207383               0.3252655
